summary: Filed a revision of the transfer-campaign probe to fix the wiring fault that left its crux comparison unresolved. The previous receipt answered the question but scored two of four comparisons incomplete, and one of them was the most important one — whether the incumbent leader granted the vote itself — so the strongest evidence for that finding rested on a raw-event citation. The fault was mine and it repeats a mistake this run made once before: a single admission alias bound to a node-2 event cannot correlate events carrying node 1, and one shared event name for two nodes' closing states cannot resolve into separate comparisons. The revised function emits its own admission event per node (v_leader_setup for the leader alongside the follower's v_lease_established) and gives each node's final state its own name (v_new_leader_state, v_old_leader_state), so every comparison pairs a result event with an admission event carrying the same node; it also adds one comparison that states the authority transfer directly by requiring the incumbent to still be the leader. Nothing else moved: same fixture, same under-lease control, same trigger carrying the follower's own term, same delivery sequence. The harness was smoke-run locally before filing and now emits the expected seven-event stream, so the revision should resolve all five comparisons instead of leaving two unresolved; if the window closes before the new receipt can be read, nothing is lost, because the interpretation already recorded on the question reaches the same conclusion (violated, defect refuted) with the raw indices 63-68 of CheckRun 96687fc34bdf45de9237914e30828d38 and states the wiring fix explicitly in its limitations. Submission validates with execution_requested=true, which puts one execution in flight at the wire.
